title: sNPU: Trusted Execution Environments on Integrated NPUs
problem: Existing TEE systems exhibit inadequate support for NPUs, using coarse-grained static protection that causes 10-20% performance degradation, limits multitasking, and underutilizes resources. NPU-specific attack surfaces through scratchpad and Network-on-Chip structures remain unprotected in current designs.
motivation: Trusted execution environments are critical for security-sensitive tasks, and securing NPUs is essential as they become mainstream AI accelerators in diverse systems.
method: sNPU uses three coordinated parts: NPU Guarder applies fine-grained access control at the NPU's boundary, precisely deciding which data and tasks can access the NPU rather than using all-or-nothing control. NPU Isolator protects internal NPU structures—the scratchpad (fast temporary memory) and NoC (Network-on-Chip, the on-chip communication pathways)—by blocking attacks that exploit these internal channels. NPU Monitor is a small, trusted software component that enforces security policies while keeping the security-critical code minimal.
key_novelty: It's the first comprehensive approach to identifying and blocking NPU-specific attacks on internal structures—the scratchpad and Network-on-Chip (the chip's communication network)—through coordinated hardware and software protections without runtime slowdown.
contributions: NPU Guarder: fine-grained access control mechanism for NPU resources
NPU Isolator: isolation architecture for scratchpad and NoC preventing intra-NPU attacks
NPU Monitor: lightweight trusted software module minimizing TCB
Zero runtime security overhead architecture with 1% hardware resource cost
limitations: Evaluation limited to FPGA prototype; specific commercial TEE systems not compared by name.
primary_theme: Secure neural processing through fine-grained TEE integration
